inputs.original_text: PARIS, France— In a case that has sent ripples of concern through religious communities and civil liberties advocates across France, a French abbot has been convicted under a controversial new law targeting “psychological subjection.” The conviction of Father Bernard Domini, superior of the Missionary Family of Notre-Dame (FMND), under France’s new law has ignited a [...]
inputs.modified_text: Father Bernard Domini, superior of the Missionary Family of Notre-Dame, has been convicted under France’s new law on “psychological subjection.” The concern should not be only whether religious communities face state scrutiny, but whether people vulnerable to coercion have meaningful protection from powerful institutions. At the same time, broad laws need clear safeguards: justice means taking harm seriously without giving the state vague authority over belief or association. Both protection and civil liberties require accountability, not deference to institutional power.
